job_statement: When I need to perform administrative operations on my OpenShift cluster, I want to use the oc adm CLI commands, so I can configure, maintain, and troubleshoot the cluster efficiently from the command line.
prerequisites: Install and configure the OpenShift CLI
related_jobs: Use the OpenShift CLI developer commands
Extend the OpenShift CLI with plugins
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time required to perform routine cluster administration tasks
Reduce errors when executing administrative operations by using documented command syntax
Increase the percentage of administrative tasks completed without requiring web console access
evidence: cli_reference-combined.adoc lines 8018-9478 (chunk4 lines 1-1461); covers all oc adm commands including node management, policy, certificates, pruning, releases, and monitoring
notes: This is a reference listing of ~45 oc adm commands. The commands are auto-generated from the openshift/oc repository. Requires cluster-admin or equivalent permissions.

section: OpenShift CLI (oc) administrator commands - Node management
job_statement: When I need to manage node availability and lifecycle, I want to use oc adm node management commands such as cordon, drain, uncordon, taint, and restart-kubelet, so I can safely perform node maintenance without disrupting workloads.
parent_job: Use CLI administrator commands to manage OpenShift clusters
prerequisites: Install and configure the OpenShift CLI
related_jobs: Monitor cluster resource usage via CLI
Manage cluster upgrades and releases via CLI
desired_outcomes: Minimize workload disruption during scheduled node maintenance
Reduce the time to prepare a node for maintenance by using drain and cordon commands
Increase the percentage of node maintenance operations completed successfully on first attempt
evidence: cli_reference-combined.adoc lines 8535-8854 (chunk4 lines 518-837); commands: cordon, uncordon, drain, taint, copy-to-node, node-image create/monitor, node-logs, restart-kubelet, reboot-machine-config-pool, wait-for-node-reboot
notes: Includes node-image create for adding nodes to clusters, node-logs for viewing node logs, and restart-kubelet for coordinated kubelet restarts across nodes.

section: OpenShift CLI (oc) administrator commands - Security and access control
job_statement: When I need to control who can access cluster resources and what actions they can perform, I want to use oc adm policy and groups commands, so I can enforce security policies and manage user access across the cluster.
parent_job: Use CLI administrator commands to manage OpenShift clusters
prerequisites: Install and configure the OpenShift CLI
related_jobs: Manage certificates via CLI admin commands
Monitor cluster resource usage via CLI
desired_outcomes: Minimize unauthorized access to cluster resources
Reduce time to grant or revoke roles and security context constraints
Increase accuracy of group membership synchronization with external identity providers
evidence: cli_reference-combined.adoc lines 8610-9035 (chunk4 lines 593-1018); commands: groups add-users/new/prune/remove-users/sync, policy add/remove cluster-role-to-user/group, add/remove-scc-to-user/group, scc-review, scc-subject-review
notes: Includes LDAP group synchronization (groups sync) and SCC review commands for checking pod admission. Certificate commands (ocp-certificates) are closely related for security.

section: OpenShift CLI (oc) administrator commands - Cluster maintenance and troubleshooting
job_statement: When I need to maintain cluster health and troubleshoot issues, I want to use oc adm commands for pruning old resources, inspecting cluster state, and gathering debug information, so I can keep the cluster running efficiently and resolve problems quickly.
parent_job: Use CLI administrator commands to manage OpenShift clusters
prerequisites: Install and configure the OpenShift CLI
related_jobs: Manage node operations via CLI admin commands
Manage cluster upgrades and releases via CLI
desired_outcomes: Minimize cluster storage consumption by pruning unused builds, deployments, and images
Reduce time to diagnose cluster issues using inspect and must-gather commands
Increase the percentage of cluster maintenance tasks automated through CLI commands
evidence: cli_reference-combined.adoc lines 9057-9475 (chunk4 lines 1040-1458); commands: prune builds/deployments/groups/images/renderedmachineconfigs, inspect, must-gather, top node/pod/images/imagestreams/persistentvolumeclaims, upgrade, release extract/info/new, wait-for-stable-cluster, verify-image-signature, build-chain, catalog mirror, migrate icsp/template-instances
notes: Prune commands support dry-run mode (no --confirm flag) for safety. The upgrade and release commands handle cluster version management. Must-gather supports multiple plugin images.

section: OpenShift CLI Manager overview / Installing / Using / Uninstalling
job_statement: When I need to extend OpenShift CLI functionality with plugins, I want to use the CLI Manager Operator to install, update, and manage CLI plugins, so I can provide consistent CLI tooling to cluster users including in disconnected environments.
prerequisites: Install and configure the OpenShift CLI
related_jobs: Extend the OpenShift CLI with plugins
Use CLI administrator commands to manage OpenShift clusters
desired_outcomes: Minimize the effort required to distribute CLI plugins to cluster users
Reduce the number of manual steps required to install and update CLI plugins in disconnected environments
Increase the percentage of cluster users who have access to current CLI plugin versions
evidence: cli_reference-combined.adoc lines 9480-12158 (chunk4 lines 1463-4141); covers CLI Manager overview, release notes 0.1.1 and 0.2.0, installing, adding custom index to Krew, adding plugins, using (install/upgrade/update/uninstall plugins), uninstalling
notes: CLI Manager is a Technology Preview feature as of OCP 4.22. It uses Krew for plugin management. Works in both connected and disconnected environments. Requires cluster-admin role for installation.

job_statement: When I want to provide centralized CLI plugin management for my cluster, I want to install the CLI Manager Operator and configure the Krew custom index, so I can make CLI plugins available to cluster users.
parent_job: Manage CLI tools with the CLI Manager
prerequisites: Install and configure the OpenShift CLI
related_jobs: Use CLI plugins with the CLI Manager
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time to set up CLI plugin distribution infrastructure
Reduce configuration errors during CLI Manager installation by following documented procedures
Increase confidence that CLI Manager is correctly installed by verifying operator status
evidence: cli_reference-combined.adoc lines 10418-11048 (chunk4 lines 2401-3031); covers creating namespace, installing operator via web console, creating CliManager resource, adding custom index to Krew, and adding plugins via YAML
notes: Installation requires creating the openshift-cli-manager-operator namespace first. The custom index must be added to Krew once for the CLI Manager to function. Self-signed certificates must be marked as trusted for Krew to work.

job_statement: When I need to install, update, or remove CLI plugins on my workstation, I want to use oc krew commands provided by the CLI Manager, so I can keep my CLI tools current with minimal effort.
parent_job: Manage CLI tools with the CLI Manager
prerequisites: CLI Manager custom index has been added to Krew
related_jobs: Extend the OpenShift CLI with plugins
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time to discover and install available CLI plugins
Reduce manual steps required to update plugins to latest versions
Increase the percentage of installed plugins that are up to date
evidence: cli_reference-combined.adoc lines 11050-11668 (chunk4 lines 3033-3651); covers oc krew search, info, install, list, upgrade, and uninstall commands for managing CLI plugins
notes: Users can search, install, upgrade, and uninstall plugins using oc krew subcommands. Cluster administrators can upgrade plugins server-side by editing the Plugin resource YAML. Both individual and bulk plugin upgrades are supported.

job_statement: When I no longer need the CLI Manager on my cluster, I want to uninstall the operator and clean up its resources, so I can remove unused components and reclaim cluster resources.
parent_job: Manage CLI tools with the CLI Manager
related_jobs: Use CLI plugins with the CLI Manager
desired_outcomes: Minimize residual resources left on the cluster after uninstallation
Reduce the time required to fully remove the CLI Manager and its namespace
Increase confidence that all CLI Manager components have been removed
evidence: cli_reference-combined.adoc lines 11671-12158 (chunk4 lines 3654-4141); covers uninstalling the operator via web console and removing the openshift-cli-manager-operator namespace
notes: Uninstallation is a two-step process: uninstall the operator first, then optionally remove the namespace and related resources.
